title: DOISST v2.1 warms 0.03-0.05 C per decade too fast at 60S-60N in 1982-2024; steps at input changes (1985, 2005, 7 July 2020) and the fixed ship adjustment cause the excess
abstract: Question: why does NOAA Daily OISST v2.1 (DOISST) warm faster in 1982-2024 than other current SST products, and is its fixed 0.14 C ship-to-buoy adjustment the cause, as Chan et al. (2026) suggested? Approach: we compared DOISST at 60S-60N with four references of different types: ESA CCI SST v3 (satellite only, daily, 1-degree points), HadSST4.2 and ERSSTv5 (in situ), and Roemmich-Gilson Argo (2005-2024). We fitted step models at the documented DOISST input-change dates, measured the ship-minus-buoy offset in iQuam in situ data, compared DOISST v2.1 with the retired v2.0, and used 198 moored buoys. Results: DOISST warms 0.044 +/- 0.005 C per decade faster than CCI (0.182 against 0.138), 0.033 faster than HadSST4.2, 0.047 faster than ERSSTv5 and 0.020 faster than Argo. The excess is a staircase of steps, not a drift: DOISST falls 0.065-0.08 C on 4 January 1985 (NOAA-9), rises 0.057-0.079 C on 1 January 2005 (sea-ice input change) and rises 0.057-0.089 C on 7 July 2020 (no documented change) against every reference. In iQuam the true ship-buoy offset was 0.088 C in 1982-1991, so the fixed 0.14 C adjustment made early DOISST about 0.04 C too cold; this adds 0.010-0.012 C per decade, 25-35% of the excess. Against CCI the excess divides into 1985-2011 steps (0.014), the ship term (0.018) and 2016-2023 steps (0.012). The excess is largest at 40-60S (0.05-0.09 C per decade), and DOISST anomalies for 2021-2023 are 0.08-0.13 C too warm relative to 1991-2020. Limitation: the references have their own errors, the cause of the 2020 step is unknown, and the ship term is an approximation whose fitted size depends on the reference.

display.caption: DOISST v2.1 minus four references at 60S-60N. (a) 12-month running mean with the documented input-change dates; (b) the warm step of 7 July 2020 in daily CCI and monthly in situ and Argo differences; (c) DOISST v2.1 minus the retired v2.0.

(a) 1982-2024 trends on matched masks (the dark bar equals the reference by construction). (b) Budget of the DOISST trend excess: steps at satellite and sea-ice changes 1985-2011, the fixed 0.14 C ship adjustment term and steps of 2016-2023, with 95% intervals.

Ship test with iQuam: (a) box-matched ship-minus-buoy offset against the fixed 0.14 C adjustment; (b) ship share of in situ super-observations; (c) implied DOISST ship bias against the observed DOISST-minus-reference offset before 2016.
